question.text: Under SEBI ICDR Regulations, which of the following categories is explicitly INELIGIBLE to be identified as a Social Enterprise for SSE registration?

answer.text: A rural healthcare NPO providing maternal services in aspirational districts
A corporate foundation set up by a listed conglomerate, a political organisation, and an infrastructure / housing company (except affordable housing)
A Section 8 company engaged in slum area development in Mumbai
An FPE enhancing small-and-marginal-farmer income in non-farm sectors

explanation.text: **The Logic:** SEBI ICDR Regulations explicitly exclude corporate foundations, political or religious organizations, professional or trade associations, and infrastructure and housing companies (except affordable housing) from being identified as a Social Enterprise, even if their activities superficially look like the 16 eligible activities. **The Trap:** Options A, C and D all map directly to the 16 eligible activities (healthcare, slum development, rural livelihood). Only Option B lists the exclusion classes. A common confusion is allowing corporate foundations — they are NOT eligible. **Cross-Exam Context:** Cross-links to Ch 3 (SSE Registration & Listing) and Ch 11 (Key Regulations). An SIA must reject an engagement where the entity is a corporate foundation seeking SSE onboarding. **Assessor's Pro-Tip:** When a corporate group approaches, verify whether the vehicle is a standalone Section 8 / trust / society vs a 'corporate foundation' arm. Check the donor pattern: if >60% funding comes from one corporate parent, treat this as a red flag even if the entity formally meets other criteria.
